newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer-Italy has equal chance to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer-Italy has equal chance to join EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that he was not opposed to Italy joining European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Asked whether he was against Italy, Tietmeyer said: "No, quite the opposite."
"Every country has the same chance (to join EMU)," he said. "Italy has the same chance as every other country."
Speaking in an EMU debate on German television, Tietmeyer also said that sustainability, not precise figures, was of primary importance for the success of the single currency.
"It's not a question of whether a country meets a particular figure on a particular date, it is a question of the long-term sustainability of the euro," he said.

Gerhard Schroeder, a leading figure in Germany's opposition Social Democrats, said in the same televised debate that the criteria for EMU membership must be met to ensure the trust of the financial markets.

"If the criteria are not held to, then people will not believe in the euro, and the financial markets will not believe in the euro," Schroeder said, adding that this could lead to interest rate hikes.
